newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish coalition allies at odds over elections.
newsitem.headline: Turkish coalition allies at odds over elections.

text.p: The Turkish government's bid for early elections was in doubt on Thursday after a marathon meeting of the junior coalition partners failed to break a deadlock over formation of an "election" government.

A leading member of the conservative True Path Party, which met late into the night on Wednesday, said his party was at odds with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on a deal to transfer power to True Path and lead the country to early elections.
MP Mehmet Gozlukaya said his faction resolved to stick to demands that Erbakan honour a promise to swap jobs with True Path leader Tansu Ciller, despite wavering by the prime minister.
"We want the prime minister's job handed over to us if the elections law is delayed. That's about the size of it. We want the prime ministership transferred in June," Gozlukaya told Reuters.

Erbakan said last weekend that he would step down by the end of this month in favour of Ciller to go to early polls but then suggested he would not quit unless early elections were a certainty. No date has been fixed for balloting.
Gozlukaya said Ciller and Erbakan were debating their differences over the power transfer. "The leaders are discussing this and will reach a result," he said.

Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, has been under intense pressure from the secularist army to crack down on religious activism. Ciller, who is also the foreign minister and was Turkey's first woman prime minister, says she could ward off the army better than the Islamists if she took power.
The head of Turkey's election board told the press this week that it could take at least six months and millions of dollars to register voters for early polls.
"There is a problem with electoral rolls. It is a technical matter out of our hands but its effect on us is that it creates an obstacle to fixing an election date," Golzukaya said.
A spokesman for Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party said on Thursday he hoped legislation that would clear the way for elections in the autumn would be passed by parliament within a month.
